exposure: Implementation of a systematic approach to reduce nulliparous cesarean birth rates
Education for health care providers and nurses on contemporary labor management guidelines
Instruction for nurses on labor support techniques (e.g., maternal position changes, use of peanut birthing ball)
outcome: Nulliparous, term, singleton, vertex cesarean birth rate
Health care provider compliance with labor management guidelines
Use of maternal position changes during labor
Use of peanut birthing ball during labor
cohort: The study participants were nulliparous women giving birth to term, singleton, vertex infants, observed in a pre-guideline period (n=434) and a post-guideline period (n=401) at two rural and one urban community hospitals.
finding: Implementing a systematic approach to care for nulliparous women was associated with a significant decrease in the term, singleton, vertex cesarean birth rate from 27.9% to 19.7%.
mod_finding: The primary finding shows a reduction in the cesarean birth rate, which is a specific mode of birth, directly demonstrating the intervention's impact on birth mode.
cross-section timing: Pre-guideline implementation period: January 1, 2015, to June 30, 2015; Post-guideline implementation period: July 1, 2016, to December 31, 2016.
